title: Microfabrication of Nanoporous Gold Patterns for Cell-material Interaction Studies
protocol: Clean substrates in Piranha solution.
Add 25 ml hydrogen peroxide to 100 ml sulfuric acid in a crystallization dish and heat to 65 °C on a hotplate.
Place microscope slides into the mixture using acid-resistant forceps for 10 min.
Treat small coverslips with air plasma at 10 W for 30 sec prior to cleaning.
Rinse cleaned samples in crystallization dishes under running deionized water for 3 min.
Blow-dry samples with a nitrogen gun over lint-free towels.
Punch 250 μm-thick silicone elastomer sheets with biopsy punches and/or incise out regions with a scalpel.
Clean the processed elastomer sheets in 70% isopropanol and dry with nitrogen gun.
Place punched sheet on a lint-free cleanroom towel and align piranha-cleaned coverslips over the stencil.
Place a piranha-cleaned microscope slide on spinning chuck.
Blow off any particulates from the glass slide with nitrogen gun.
Dispense 1.5 ml of adhesion promoter onto the glass slide using a plastic pipette.
Spin the slide at 500 rpm for 5 sec and then at 1,500 rpm for 30 sec to spread the promoter.
Bake the slide on a hotplate at 115 °C for 7 min.
Let the slide cool for 5 min.
Dispense 4 ml of photoresist onto the glass slide (3-inch by 1-inch).
Spin the slide with the same protocol as used for the adhesion promoter to spread the photoresist.
Bake the photoresist on a hotplate at 115 °C for 1.5 min.
Let it cool for 10 min.
Expose the photoresist-coated slide with UV light (intensity: 22 mW/cm²) through a transparency mask for 15 sec.
Bake the photoresist on a hotplate at 115 °C for 1.5 min.
Wait for 45 min.
Dissolve the exposed photoresist in the developer for at least 3.5 min.
Rinse thoroughly with DI water.
Inspect the developed patterns under an optical microscope.
Load the samples into a sputtering machine that can independently deposit gold, silver, and chrome.
Sputter-clean the samples for 90 sec at 50 W under 25 mTorr argon processing atmosphere before starting metal deposition.
Sputter chrome for 10 minutes at 300 W under 10 mTorr argon.
Sputter gold for 90 seconds at 400 W under 10 mTorr argon.
Co-sputter gold and silver for 10 minutes with silver at 200 W and Au power at 100 W.
Turn off the gold sputter source approximately 10 seconds before turning off the silver sputter source.
Sonicate photoresist-coated samples in ~180 ml of photoresist stripper for 10 cycles of 20 seconds sonication and a 2-minute pause between each cycle.
Rinse the samples with DI water.
Dry the samples with a nitrogen gun.
Inspect the metal patterns under a microscope.
Peel the elastomer stencil from non-photoresist-coated samples using two tweezers to reveal the deposited metal.
Fill a 200 ml glass beaker with 170 ml of nitric acid (70%) and maintain the solution temperature at 55 °C on a hotplate.
Treat small coverslips with air plasma at 10 W for 30 seconds prior to immersion into nitric acid.
Place 1-inch by 3-inch microscope slides into the beaker using acid-resistant forceps and dealloy them for 15 minutes.
Rinse dealloyed samples by successively immersing them in two beakers filled with fresh DI water three times.
Store samples in DI water, replacing the water daily for at least a week.
Blow-dry samples with a nitrogen gun over lint-free towels before use.
Load samples onto a clean silicon wafer in rapid thermal processing equipment.
Adjust temperature to between 200 °C and 450 °C and ramp rate to 10 °C/sec.
Expose the samples to the prescribed temperature for 10 min under nitrogen ambient.
Let the chamber cool (<100 °C) before removing the samples.
Place samples on a hotplate for thermal treatment alternatively.
Place np-Au samples in polystyrene dishes and treat with air plasma at 10 W for 30 sec.
Transfer treated np-Au samples to 24-well tissue culture plates.
Add 500 μl complete culture media (Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin/streptomycin) to each well.
Store the samples in a humidified incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 until cells are seeded (<1 hr).
Maintain cells of interest in T75 flasks with culture media.
Passage cells when they reach 70% confluence.
Remove media from the flask and wash twice with 10 ml phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Add 2 ml of 1x Trypsin/EDTA to the flask.
Incubate until the cells detach (~5 min).
Add 3 ml fresh media to the detached cells.
Centrifuge at 1,200 rpm for 3 min.
Aspirate supernatant and suspend the pellet in 2 ml media.
Remove spent media from the wells.
Seed cells onto glass coverslips at a density of 25,000 cells/cm² with a final volume of 1 ml.
Shake the culture plate forward-back and right-left to ensure uniform coating of cells over the samples.
Incubate cells until analysis while inspecting daily.
Remove spent media from wells.
Wash cells twice with PBS.
Fix cells in 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS for 15 min.
Prepare staining solution of 300 nM Alexa Fluor 488 phalloidin in PBS with 1% bovine serum albumin.
Wash cells twice with PBS.
Permeabilize cells in 500 μl 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS for 5 min.
Wash cells twice with PBS and transfer them to clean wells.
Blot 50 - 200 μl staining solution onto the samples and store in dark for 20 min.
Wash cells with PBS.
Counter-stain with 3 nM of DAPI in PBS for 5 min.
Wash cells with PBS.
Dip cells in deionized water before mounting on glass cover slides.
Mount samples with mounting media and seal with clear nail polish.
Acquire images of np-Au samples using a scanning electron microscope at 50,000X magnification and 10 kV electron energy.
Capture composite cell images using an inverted fluorescence microscope at 10X magnification.
Process images to determine pore and cell morphology in ImageJ.
Split images into individual channels if applicable.
Convert images to 8-bit format.
Subtract the background from the images.
Smooth images by median filtering.
Adjust threshold manually or using built-in algorithms to highlight pores and cell bodies/nuclei.
Use watershed command to separate merged pores or cells.
Set particle analysis parameters in ImageJ.
Execute particle analysis to extract number of particles, average area, and percent coverage by particles.
Use DAPI-stained cell images for counting cells.
Quantify percent cell coverage using phalloidin-stained cell images.
Modify included macro files to perform batch analysis of multiple images.
